text.p: Firefighters on Tuesday fully contained a big wildfire that has burned for more than a week in California's scenic Los Padres National Forest, officials said.
"We are happy that we are at 100 percent containment," Rich Tobin, a national forest spokesman, said on Tuesday evening.
However, he said there was no estimate of when the fire would be fully controlled, meaning it no longer posed any threat.
The U.S. Forest Service also announced that it was offering a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person who set the fire eight days ago.
The fire has charred 25,590 acres (10,350 hectares) of trees and brush near Big Sur, an area popular with campers and hikers about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.

"We anticipate that the acreage will continue to climb because we are burning out areas of unburned vegetation within the fire perimeter," Tobin said. This was done partly because of the danger that unburned areas could ignite and spread the fire outside fire lines, he said.
The fire destroyed five homes, nine outbuildings, two travel trailers and two vehicles. Firefighting costs were expected to reach $6.3 million, Tobin said.
He said the fire had been difficult to fight because it burned in very steep, rugged terrain with few roads.
About 1,000 firefighters have left the fire in the last two days, leaving behind about 1,500, backed by 77 fire engines, five air tankers and nine helicopters, Tobin said.
Six firefighters have been injured battling the blaze, mainly by falls and bee stings, he added.
